new-york-hudson-valley-rides-north-fork-.speedBand: 50–80 km/h riding core, local limits always win

sections.advice: This High point near Mendham → Food stop near Shrewsbury stretch is for rhythm and scenery. Keep your head up, let the view breathe, and resist turning every open bend into a target. Stop once properly rather than half-stopping everywhere.

Food stop near Shrewsbury → Sea Girt is the logistics leg. Watch junctions, villages and speed changes, then let the roadbook do its job: move you out of the clutter without spending your best attention too early.

Scenic stretch in Old Bethpage → Photo stop near Fort Salonga is the technical section. Hairpins, gradients and mixed traffic can stack up quickly; use low drama inputs, stay wide of centre lines and expect buses or riders appearing exactly where optimism says they will not.
Photo stop near Fort Salonga → Kearny can flow quickly, but only if you keep village limits and junction sightlines sacred. Fast connectors are where rides get untidy when fatigue creeps in.

safetyMarkers.note: Respect posted limits and assume enforcement near villages, viewpoints and main-road joins.
A line-crossing or merge area where relaxed sightseeing traffic can behave unpredictably.
Watch shade, leaves, gravel wash and damp patches; conditions decide the pace.
